# Judith Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_002_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Eighteen years into his reign — on the twenty-second day of the first month — Nebuchadnezzar made his move. The time had come to do exactly what he had promised: vengeance on all the western lands.

**2** He gathered his officers and nobles and laid out his plan. In his own words, he spelled out what he intended to do to every nation that had defied him.

**3** The verdict was unanimous: total destruction for everyone who had ignored his command.

**4** When the council was over, Nebuchadnezzar summoned Holofernes — supreme commander of the Assyrian armies, the second most powerful man in the empire — and gave him his orders:

**5** "This is the decree of the great king, lord of all the earth. Go. Take with you a hundred and twenty thousand infantry and twelve thousand cavalry — veterans, men who trust their own strength.

**6** March west. They defied me. Now they will answer for it.

**7** Demand that every city render earth and water as tokens of submission. I am coming for them in my fury. My army will cover the face of the earth. I will hand everything over to be plundered.

**8** The dead will fill every ravine and wadi. The rivers will run with corpses. Every valley and mountain pass will be piled with their bodies.

**9** Every survivor I will drag to the ends of the earth in chains.

**10** Go ahead of me. Seize their lands. If they surrender, keep them under guard for the day of reckoning.

**11** If they resist — no mercy. Put them to the sword and take everything.

**12** I swear by my life and my crown: I have said it, and it will be done by my own hand.

**13** You will follow my orders to the letter. No deviation. No delay."

**14** Holofernes went straight from the palace to his commanders, generals, and officers.

**15** He assembled the strike force his lord had ordered — a hundred and twenty thousand infantry, twelve thousand mounted archers —

**16** and organized them into full battle formation.

**17** An enormous baggage train followed: camels, donkeys, mules beyond counting, and livestock — sheep, cattle, goats — enough to provision an empire on the march.

**18** Every soldier was fully supplied. Gold and silver flowed from the royal treasury.

**19** The army moved out — Holofernes at the head of a force that blanketed the western landscape with chariots and cavalry and marching columns of elite infantry.

**20** Behind the army came a vast mixed crowd — hangers-on, camp followers, auxiliaries — as numberless as locusts, as the sand of the sea.

**21** Three days out of Nineveh they reached the plain of Bectileth. They camped near the mountain on the left flank of Upper Cilicia.

**22** Then Holofernes led his combined force — foot soldiers, cavalry, chariots — up into the hill country.

**23** He laid waste to Phud and Lud. He stripped the Rassites and the Ishmaelites who lived along the desert edge south of the Chellaean territory.

**24** He crossed the Euphrates, swept through Mesopotamia, and tore down every walled city along the Abron river all the way to the coast.

**25** He seized Cilicia, killing every man who stood against him, then pushed south toward the Japheth frontier facing Arabia.

**26** He encircled the Midianite camps, torched their tents, and drove off their flocks.

**27** He came down into the Damascus plain at harvest time and burned every field, butchered the livestock, looted the towns, and cut down every able-bodied man with the sword.

**28** Panic ran ahead of him along the coast. Sidon, Tyre, Sur, Okina, Jamnia — the coastal cities shook. Azotus and Ascalon were terrified.
